name: Seerr Search
description: Adds an "Available on request" section under the search results of the Jellyfin web client. Titles come from Seerr, and each request is created as the Seerr account linked to the signed-in Jellyfin user: no second sign-in, no password, and Seerr's quotas and permissions keep applying per user. The Seerr API key stays on the server.
overview: Seerr results under the Jellyfin search, with a Request button.

versions.changelog: First public version. The plugin works as before for existing installations (same settings, same behavior), and is now meant for other people's servers. - Configuration page in the Jellyfin dashboard, in English and French (follows the interface language). A first install, with nothing configured, does nothing and says so on that page. The API key is never loaded back into the form. - English and French interface for the search section, following each user's Jellyfin language. The Seerr language is the user's own unless one is set in the settings (no built-in French default any more). - New: choose what users who have no Seerr account see (a message, your own message, or nothing). - New: working "Request in 4K" button when 4K requests are allowed. - New: the import button only imports the accounts that are missing, and says how many are not linked. - New: the connection test also checks the API key and counts the unlinked accounts. - Security: the poster relay now requires a Jellyfin session (it was open to anyone who could reach the server) and always answers with an image type; posters are fetched with the user's token. - Security: URLs typed in the settings are validated (plain http/https, no credentials, no query string); other schemes can no longer be used for server requests, redirects or links. - Security: per-user rate limits on searches, requests and posters; search text length limit. - Security: the script is not injected until Seerr is configured. - Fix: a "409 Conflict" from Seerr (already requested) is no longer confused with "user not linked". - Fix: the unused "request all seasons" setting was removed. - Fix: language codes are normalized the way TMDB expects (`fr-ca` becomes `fr-CA`).
